summary.title: Building Secure and Reliable Systems
summary.one_liner: A free online book from Google covering how to design, implement, and maintain systems that are both secure and reliable, organized into five parts from introductory material to organization and culture.
keywords: how to design systems that are secure and reliable
takeaways: Security and reliability share design concerns such as simplicity, evolution, and resilience, and can be considered together.
Least privilege, understandability, and designing for changing threats are core system design principles covered in Part II.
Implementation topics include secure code, testing, static analysis, and safe deployment practices.
Maintenance topics cover disaster planning, crisis management, recovery, and investigating systems and logging.
The book ends with organizational guidance on roles, responsibilities, and building a healthy security culture.
summary.summary: This page is the table of contents for Google's free online book Building Secure and Reliable Systems. It lists five parts: introductory material, designing systems, implementing systems, maintaining systems, and organization and culture, with chapters including case studies on safe proxies, a publicly trusted CA, and the Chrome security team. The page itself only shows chapter and section titles, so it gives an outline of topics rather than detailed content. The listing describes the book as very complete.
